problem_type: Timeout fixtures assume startup side effects precede a short deadline
symptom: Gate self-test returns its expected timeout result then fails reading slow.pid with ENOENT.
direct_cause: The 1500ms production deadline can terminate node:test/tsx startup before fixture PID or counter writes.
class_root: Timeout policy tests treated elapsed startup time as evidence of fixture readiness.
affected_population: Synchronous read retry success-after-timeout and exhausted-timeout self-tests

external_sources.purpose: Readiness and paired descendant liveness assertions.
Short native timeout tests need no user-code side effects.
Short startup deadline tests assert signal rather than fixture side effects.

invariants: A tree timeout assertion requires two distinct valid PIDs alive before the deadline fires and gone before success.
Fixture startup delay is excluded from the test-controlled deadline; production startup deadlines are unchanged.
Synchronous retry policy cannot depend on a counter being written by a process that may time out during startup.
PID readiness files are published by rename only after the complete PID has been written.

door_reduction.why_not: The two existing test files exercise different production boundaries. Both now enter readyTreeTimeout; the retry file shares one observedTimeout wrapper across its two cases. Production callers remain unchanged.

generality_proof: Both test files converge on one readiness and liveness owner; neither a missing PID nor a skipped assertion can produce success. PID files are written by the processes themselves. Real termination remains in the production runner, including under tree-kill mutation.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Freeze the test deadline until readiness, check two live PIDs, trigger timeout with real cleanup scheduling, then require both PIDs gone. Publish complete PID records atomically before exposing readiness.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: related timeout softening and real failure

same_class_entry_points.evidence: observedTimeout requires real ready tree termination; synchronous policy uses explicit parent-owned attempt observations.
Same shared tree observation and explicit parent-owned call count, no child startup counter.

recurrence.reason: Startup latency varies by CPU, IO, memory, runner layers and future machines; all three cases had this assumption.
same_class_scan: Searched all 177 scripts/**/*.node-test.mjs and *.test.mjs for timeout/budget, PID and counter writes.
Checked processTree.node-test.mjs and _test-temp.node-test.mjs condition-based readiness; short pure timeout assertions have no side-effect prerequisite.
door-map runNode runRelatedTests execGhReadSync --roots=scripts --include-tests: 13 doors/24 call sites; new shared readiness owner has 2 doors.

prevention.invariant: Two valid distinct real fixture processes must be observed alive before the deadline and gone after it.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing readiness, invalid PID, premature exit or surviving descendant fails the test; cleanup never substitutes for assertions.
prevention.strategy: Centralize fixture startup and paired liveness checks, use the built-in test clock only for the deadline, and separate synchronous retry policy from native timeout integration.

legacy_paths.rationale: Removed inline slow fixture and HANG_SCRIPT/counter assumptions in the same change; no parallel old fixture remains.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency migration; uses existing Node test mock timers, real runner and process tree utilities.

migration: No product data or production runner migration. Only self-test fixtures and observations change.
residual_risks: Validation is macOS/Node 24; Windows PID cleanup semantics remain unverified locally.
Synchronous retry policy uses an explicit command-boundary double; native exec timeout has a separate real integration assertion.
